$comment: Single source of truth for every number and claim published on the site. THE RULE: no figure is ever typed into markup — pages import from here, so a number that appears on four pages exists once. Every leaf carries a `source`; anything not independently verified carries `verified: false` and shows up in your risk review. If you need a number that isn't here, add it WITH a source or leave a TODO — never estimate.

founder.$comment: MOVED. The founder is ONE record, in src/data/authors.json — the registry an /author/<slug> page already renders and that check-source-rules already holds every byline to. It was here as well, which meant two places to change a name and two identities in the entity graph (the author page emitted #author-founder while every other page pointed at #founder). src/data/site.ts → FOUNDER reads the registry entry named by FOUNDER_SLUG; nothing reads this key.

company.$comment: The company's own facts — the Key Facts table on /about renders one row per key below, and OMITS any row whose value is still TODO (marketing/page-guidelines.md § 3: a row the site cannot fill honestly is omitted, never estimated). BaseLayout's Organization node reads legalName, founded, headquarters and social the same way, and leaves each out while it says TODO — an empty string in JSON-LD is worse than an absent field, and the entity-hygiene invariant fails it. Every value carries a source, like every other figure on this site. ACTIONS A-L04 checks for the TODOs, A-L13 requires the owner to approve the facts in writing before the page goes live, and A-Q03 re-confirms them quarterly.

legalName.$comment: The registered legal name, if it differs from the trading name. The Organization node’s `legalName`.

type.$comment: The category phrase a buyer would use, e.g. "freight forwarding software company". The entity sentence’s `<category>`.

founded.$comment: The founding year, four digits. Becomes the Organization node’s `foundingDate`.

coreOffering.$comment: What the company sells, one line. Keep in step with the `offering` on the primary solutions page.

pricing.$comment: One line on how pricing works — a published from-price, "on request", or the model.

contractTerms.$comment: One line, e.g. "month-to-month, 30 days’ notice". The most-asked commercial question after price.

customersServed.$comment: A confirmed count. Omitted from the table while TODO — never estimated.

projectsDelivered.$comment: A confirmed count. Omitted from the table while TODO.

headquarters.$comment: The Organization node’s PostalAddress. All three parts, or the address is left out of the schema entirely — a partial address is a worse claim than none.

services.$comment: What the company does, one entry per service. The Key Facts "Services" row lists the names; /about § 2 renders each as an H3 with its two sentences from src/data/about.json → services.

communication.$comment: Channels and response time, one line, e.g. "email and shared Slack; replies within one business day".

notableClients.$comment: One entry per named client, each { name, permission, source }. A client is RENDERED ONLY when permission is true — naming a customer who has not agreed is the fastest way to lose them, and a template cannot judge that for you. Entries without permission stay here as a record and never reach the page.

competitors.$comment: The rivals a buyer compares this company with, as names. Keep in step with src/data/intent.json → competitors — check-parity rule 6 fails a commit where the two lists differ, because one is what the pages may name and the other is what the scripts watch in Search Console. Filled from marketing/landscape.md.

social.$comment: The company's OWN profiles, as absolute URLs, and only accounts that exist and are active — these become the Organization node's `sameAs`, which is how an engine corroborates the entity. A dead profile there weakens every other claim. The founder's personal profile belongs on the Person node (company.founder.linkedin), not here.
